Global Metadata: A serene traditional Japanese instrumental piece, 70 BPM, contemplative and spare. Built around the koto (13-string plucked zither) and the shakuhachi (bamboo end-blown flute), with a soft taiko drum pulse far in the distance. The koto plays a delicate plucked melody with subtle ornaments, the shakuhachi answers with a breathy, airy, flowing line, they trade phrases over a very light sparse texture, then settle into a calm meditative ending. Production profile: intimate, hushed traditional recording, warm wooden koto tone, breathy natural shakuhachi, deep resonant taiko, studio mastering with generous dynamic range.

This is a purely instrumental track. There is no singing, no voice, no lyrics, no spoken words, no chanting. The piece is performed entirely by the instruments described. No human voice appears anywhere.

Arrangement: Intro, the koto alone plucks a delicate melody with subtle ornaments. Section one, the shakuhachi enters with a breathy flowing line answering the koto. Section two, the two instruments trade phrases over a sparse texture with a distant soft taiko pulse. Section three, both weave together gently. Outro, a calm meditative ending and a soft fade.
